newsitem.title: FRANCE: Debray wants Frenchman released in Bolivia.
newsitem.headline: Debray wants Frenchman released in Bolivia.

text.p: Ex-Marxist revolutionary Regis Debray, once Bolivia's most famous political prisoner, on Monday joined a campaign for the release of a fellow Frenchman held in the Andean country on subversion and terrorism charges.
Debray wrote in the newspaper Le Monde that Alain Mesili, a 47-year-old mountain guide jailed since February 1995, was "the only French political prisoner in Latin America".
Danielle Mitterrand, the widow of president Francois Mitterrand, and French Senator Pierre Biarnes have repeatedly called on Bolivian authorities to release Mesili.

Mesili is accused of chauffeuring members of an armed group which carried out a 1990 attack on a U.S. Marine residence in La Paz in which a Bolivian policeman was killed. He is also accused of renting a flat in which a Bolivian industrialist was held and later killed when police stormed it.
Mesili has denied both charges, arguing that he was in hospital the day of the La Paz attack and in Peru later.

He was arrested in 1994 on a stopover at Miami airport and extradited to Bolivia the following year. Debray called Mesili a pawn in a diplomatic game, saying U.S. authorities handed him over in exchange for a prominent Bolivian drug trafficker.
Debray said Mesili may have been thoughtless in making friends with leftists who committed crimes.
"Mesili, a mountain guide familiar with ice and the sky, is neither a murderer nor a terrorist. Blood is not his cup of tea," he wrote.
"Bolivia's democratic government would do itself a great honour in releasing Alain Mesili -- whether the final decision is an amnesty, a pardon or an expulsion," Debray wrote.

Debray was arrested in Bolivia after visiting Ernesto "Che" Guevara and his group of Cuban guerrillas in the jungle. He was in prison when the Bolivian army crushed the guerrillas and killed Guevara in 1967.
He was released after pressure from the late General Charles de Gaulle and later became a presidential adviser to Mitterrand.
